audit.whatIsWrong: 'max-ranked Blinding Shot has a 6-second blind duration that covers almost the full Counter Strike dodge window'.
audit.why: No blind in the game lasts six seconds, and Teemo's Q is also on a flat 7-second cooldown at every rank — so a player who believes this will bait Counter Strike, throw Q, and expect a window that does not exist. I removed the invented number rather than replacing it with another one, because blind duration is not in the kit file and I will not assert a figure I cannot source.
audit.corrected: The window is Counter Strike's own cooldown — 17s at rank 1 down to 9s at rank 5 — not the length of your blind. Bait E, let the dodge expire, then commit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Q cooldown flat 7; blind duration not in the file)

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is treated as a stun to be dodged, without stating what it actually does to Teemo specifically.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Jax's combat prowess allows him to dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration.' Teemo's entire damage output — Toxic Shot poison, Nashor's on-hit, everything — rides on basic attacks. Counter Strike therefore does not reduce Teemo's damage, it zeroes it. That is the single most important sentence in this matchup and it is not written anywhere.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, and every point of Teemo damage is a basic attack. While it is up your DPS is zero, not reduced — so fight the cooldown, never the ability.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grandmaster-at-Arms is described as 'stacking bonus stats on extended fights' with no mention of what those stats are.
audit.why: Riot's text: the active 'increas[es] his Armor and Magic Resist for a short duration'. Magic resist — against a champion whose damage is almost entirely magic. That is a direct counter to Teemo's damage profile at level 6, and it explains the Level 6 row being sided to Jax far better than the boilerplate about shroom nets does.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster-at-Arms' active gives Armour and Magic Resist on demand, and your damage is magic — his R is a defensive answer to you, not just a damage steroid.

audit.why: Data Dragon names Jax's R 'Grandmaster-at-Arms'. 'Grandmaster's Might' is the retired name and it appears 297 times across champ-data, so this is a repo-wide problem rather than a one-off typo here.
sources: repo-wide string count: 297 occurrences of the old name

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Land Blinding Shot before Jax's Leap Strike lands so his Counter Strike autos miss during the stun window'.
audit.why: Counter Strike's stun is an ability effect and a blind does not touch it, and the ability itself contains no autos to blind. The sentence prescribes a sequence that does nothing.
audit.corrected: Fight the Counter Strike cooldown instead: it dodges every auto you throw, so commit only while it is down.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Blinding Shot' throughout; 'Noxious Traps' and 'Leap Strikes' were flagged by the packet but are correct plural/verb forms of the real names.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is the real name of Teemo's Q. The other two packet flags are false positives.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart; leave Noxious Traps and Leap Strikes alone.

audit.why: Trinity Force then Rageblade as his two-item takeover, and the 52.81% over 640 games, are consistent with a lane Teemo wins early and loses late. No change.

edits.after: Jax has no gap-close yet and must walk up to last-hit — land Blinding Dart early to show him that every auto trade costs him a DPS window and sets the poke tempo.

edits.after: Commit only when Counter Strike is down — 17s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5 — because it dodges every auto

edits.after: Bait or wait out Blinding Dart then Leap Strike in so Counter Strike's dodge and stun land on you while you cannot auto back

edits.before: Counter Strike is now live and Jax can Leap Strike then stun, but Blinding Shot still blind his autos during the dodge window — this is a learning-each-other-out stage where both patterns partially cancel.
edits.after: Counter Strike is live and it dodges basic attacks outright, so your entire Toxic Shot output drops to zero while it runs — this is a learning-each-other-out stage where both patterns partially cancel.

edits.before: Max-ranked Blinding Shot covers nearly the full Counter Strike dodge timer, so when you bait his E and fire Q he auto-attacks thin air through the stun window — your poison kite loop is fully online.
edits.after: Bait Counter Strike, let the dodge window expire, then Blinding Dart and poison him while E sits on its 13-to-9 second cooldown — that dead window is where your entire kite loop lives.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are your best control window: max-ranked Blinding Shot has a 6-second blind duration that covers almost the full Counter Strike dodge window, so baiting his E and then blinding him means his stun whiffs on misses and his follow-up autos deal nothing. Layer mushrooms on the tribush and both river entrances now — Jax cannot take a fight on a shroom-slowed tile without burning Leap Strike to escape the slow, which is the same ability he needs to stick to you. At 6 his Grandmaster's Might passive starts stacking bonus stats on extended fights, so keep trades short: Q-poison-retreat, never stand still long enough for him to chain E into a prolonged R-empowered slugfest.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are your best control window, but be exact about why: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, and every point of damage you own is a basic attack, so while it is up your output is zero rather than reduced. Fight its cooldown — 17 seconds at rank 1 down to 9 at rank 5 — not the ability. Bait it out, let the dodge expire, then blind and poison him while E is dead. Layer mushrooms on the tribush and both river entrances now — Jax cannot take a fight on a shroom-slowed tile without burning Leap Strike to escape the slow, which is the same ability he needs to stick to you. At 6 the Grandmaster-at-Arms active hands him Armour and Magic Resist on demand, and your damage is magic, so keep trades short: blind, poison, retreat.

edits.before: Once Jax completes Trinity Force his burst pattern genuinely threatens your HP pool in one blink-stun-W sequence, and his Rageblade second item makes extended duels essentially unwinnable for you — do not 1v1 a two-item Jax in an open side lane. Your job is shroom-wall split-push: carpet the lane bushes, river path, and jungle entries with Noxious Traps so he cannot approach safely without revealing himself, take plates at range, and disengage through the mushroom wall the moment he pops flash or Leap Strikes in. In teamfights your role is Blinding Shot onto whichever Jax target is diving your carries, not fighting him directly.

edits.before: From 6 the shroom net makes his half of the map hostile terrain. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Jax's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: From 6 your shrooms make his half hostile, but Grandmaster-at-Arms gives him Armour and Magic Resist on demand — your magic damage drops.

edits.after: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — 17s at rank 1 down to 9s; it dodges every auto you own. Bait it, then commit. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Repo-wide naming problem worth a sweep: 'Grandmaster's Might' (Jax's retired R name) appears 297 times across champ-data; Data Dragon 16.15.1 calls it 'Grandmaster-at-Arms'. I only changed the instance inside this matchup. Separately, the invented '6-second blind duration' in the mid text is the kind of number that gets a player killed — Teemo's blind duration is not in the kit file, so I removed the claim rather than substituting a figure I could not source.
